Yes, I'm happy with that logic.

Right now, after 12 mints, the leader board displays 11 tickets and 11 commissions. Perfect.

However!

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
At this point, we have completed 12 mints, so that should amount to 12 tickets & 12 x $5 commissions.

**Even if no referral code is used, a ticket and commission are still issued**.

Currently, **when a code is used**, it is accurately reflected on the leaderboards/NFT attributes. Perfect.

If **no referral code is used**, the ticket and commission are assigned at random.
(B**ut they must still be reflected on the leaderboard/NFT attributes**.)

I believe that since your most recent fix, the randomly assigned tickets from the last 2 mints have been reflected on the leaderboard/NFT attributes. Great.
However, the missing tickets have not been backfilled.

The commissions from these purchases without a code are also still not reflected on the leaderboard/NFT attributes.

In my screenshot, you will see that I have an NFT showing 2 tickets but only 1 x $5 commission. That should not be possible because each ticket includes a $5 commission.

Also, in my leaderboard screenshot, only 7 tickets and 5 x $5 commissions are accounted for out of 12 total mints.
Whether or not a referral code is used, 12 mints should result in 12 tickets and 12 x $5 commissions.

execution.observed_behavior: After the target-specific fix claim, the client reports that randomly assigned tickets from the last two mints were reflected on the leaderboard and NFT attributes.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
That plan makes sense.
Choosing **Pinata + Lit Protocol** is actually an excellent UX approach.

**The simple flow would be:**
*[ACCOUNT_001] You place the PDF on* \*Pinata (IPFS)\*\*, allowing it to be taken down later if necessary.
*[ACCOUNT_001] The NFT* \*metadata does NOT point straight to the PDF\*\*.
*[ACCOUNT_001] Instead, the metadata directs users to a* \*gated viewer page\*\*.
*[ACCOUNT_001] That viewer uses* \*Lit Protocol\*\* to automatically verify NFT ownership before decrypting and displaying the PDF.
[ACCOUNT_001] From the user’s perspective, the experience is seamless: open link → ownership is verified → PDF appears, with no manual actions required.

**Regarding the PDF:**
You only need to send me the completed PDF.
I can either:
[ACCOUNT_001] Upload it to Pinata on your behalf, using your account or mine, or
[ACCOUNT_001] Handle the integration if you would rather upload it yourself and provide the CID.

Both options work, and the gating logic remains unchanged.

value_updates.book_access_link_target: Lit Protocol gated viewer with automatic NFT ownership verification
